hook: This file assumes you have at least heard of the Church of the Broken God, catalogued here as GOI-004: a faith that wants its shattered god put back together. The anomaly itself is a Greek beach where lightning and tides turn out machines and carvings. Its real trick is the layout, which shows you several versions of the containment section in turn, with the object class changing as you go.
whyItMatters: It is a good example of a Group of Interest story: the anomaly is a place, but the plot is driven by factions, scripture and shifting alliances, with the Foundation, the Global Occult Coalition and the Horizon Initiative all in play. SCP-610 looms in the background as the larger threat, named from the very first set of procedures. Together with the Thaumiel label, that tells you the stakes are global from the start.
thingsToNotice: Follow the object class as it shifts, and notice that each version of the procedures is written by an organization that understands a little more about what it is dealing with. The excerpt from the Book of Rites is worth reading as world-building in its own right, written in a scriptural cadence that contrasts with the report voice. Don't skip the footnotes; the verses they quote give the timeline a pressure the main text never states outright. By the end, the question is less what the beach makes than who the Foundation is prepared to work with.

related.note: The threat the whole file is bracing against; it is named throughout.
Another k-class-scenario entry where the Foundation's usual secrecy comes under heavy strain.
